title: CYBRIK Suite W2-D model-inference + alert-summarization contract packet — compatibility/version manifest
description: Inventory and compatibility record for the W2-D AI-inference contract packet. ADDITIVE to, and DISJOINT from, the accepted v0.1 cross-product packet (cybrik-suite-contract-packet.v1.manifest.json): it introduces a new cybrik.model-* / cybrik.ai.* namespace and REUSES accepted primitives (common-defs, data-marking, envelope) by $ref without modifying them. Every member here is PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED at v0.1.0. No product may implement any member until a separate Founder gate (Gate W2-D) accepts it; this document does NOT accept anything and is NOT an ADR-0001 immutable bundle tag. $id uses the RFC 2606 .example documentation domain; it is an identifier, not an endpoint.
mcp_scope: OUT OF SCOPE. This packet defines no MCP server/tool/action contract and grants a model no tool/function/agent authority. Tool execution remains governed by the accepted Tool-Fabric packet (ADR-0004); MCP mapping notes there are unchanged.

adr_basis.role: versioning/format-pin policy (D1, D4, D5, D6); this packet stays v0.1.0 PROPOSED and is never a bundle tag.

model-runtime seam (G3): provider-neutral CYBRIK-owned adapter over Ollama/vLLM/llama.cpp; model gets no credential/database/tool/shell authority; constrained structured output + streaming. This packet is the contract realization of that accepted seam.

CloudEvents-style envelope (E1), workload identity (E2), conditional correlation (E6), naming (E7). Inference lifecycle events reuse the accepted envelope; identity/authority is never a model-populated field.

adr_out_of_scope.reason: Tool execution authority / capability registry / approval — a SEPARATE accepted packet. This packet carries no capability, delegation, approval, tool, or action-authorization field. The inference seam and the tool-execution seam are deliberately disjoint.
Durable agent orchestration / bus choice — NOT decided here; the AsyncAPI delta declares no servers or bindings (mirrors ADR-0006 E4).
Org-hierarchy contract delta is PROPOSED — NOT APPLIED. org_scope here is opaque/advisory only and does not depend on that unapplied delta.

reuses_accepted_unmodified.note: These accepted v0.1 members are referenced by $ref and are NOT modified, re-versioned, or re-stated by this packet. Backward compatibility of the accepted packet is preserved.

backward_compatibility.namespace: Disjoint: schema ids cybrik.model-*/cybrik.alert-summarization-*; event types cybrik.ai.<entity>.<action>.v<major> (ADR-0006 E7). No accepted id, event type, or channel is redefined.
backward_compatibility.soc_native_compatibility: Alert summarization consumes SOC alert truth by DIGEST-BOUND objectRef to soc.alert / soc.alert_snapshot (the accepted cybrik.soc.alert_snapshot.created payload). SOC remains the owner of alerts (repository boundary preserved); no SOC schema is changed. No new obligation is placed on any accepted member.

trust_invariants.note: Fail-closed trust invariants. Some are STRUCTURAL (enforced by the JSON Schemas and exercised by fixtures); others are RUNTIME-ONLY (the platform MUST enforce; JSON Schema constrains shape only). Both products MUST implement identical outcomes.
structural: TI-1 No wire lock-in / no vendor pinning: additionalProperties=false on every request/result/error, and the model is named only by a policy-selected model_class token — there is no vendor, provider, endpoint, api_key, or concrete model field to pin. Ollama/Qwen/OpenAI-envelope details are adapter metadata only.

TI-2 No tool/agent/action authority: no capability, delegation_ref, approval_id, tool, or mcp field exists in any inference payload, and capability.tool_calling is const 'disabled'. A model gets no execution authority through this seam (ADR-0002 G3; disjoint from ADR-0004).
TI-3 Fail-closed redaction: redaction_policy is required and redaction_policy.on_unresolved is const 'deny' — a caller can never request that unredacted sensitive content reach a model.
TI-4 Mandatory bounds: token limits (max_input/output/context_tokens) and deadline_seconds are required on every request; data_marking is required on every request and result.
TI-5 Replay control: idempotency_key minLength 16 on every mutating request; it is not authority after the correlated deadline.

TI-6 Cross-tenant guard: actor.tenant_id is required at the authorization site; the platform derives authoritative tenant/actor/org from the credential and rejects mismatch (advisory body fields never elevate).

TI-7 Refusal/fallback are surfaced, not dropped: outcome enumerates refused/filtered with required reasons; a fallback substitution is recorded via fallbackInfo (feature-flag/health/capacity fallback is explicit).
TI-8 Grounded, referenced context: alert summarization references alerts by digest-bound objectRef (minItems 1), never inlines SOC-owned content; an empty alert set is unsummarizable.
runtime_only: TR-1 Marking non-downgrade: a result's data_marking MUST be >= the input marking (union of alert markings for summarization); inference never lowers sensitivity. Schema cannot compare marking lattices; the platform MUST.
TR-2 Feature negotiation fail-closed: a requested_features token not in the resolved class's capability.supported_features MUST be denied (error_class 'unsupported_feature'), never silently ignored.
TR-3 Health fail-closed: an absent/stale/unrecognized cybrik.model-health signal MUST be treated as 'unavailable'; no routing to an unknown-health class.

TR-4 Budget/limit clamping: the platform clamps request limits/deadline to the resolved class ceilings and never above them; exceeding a budget yields a typed error (over_input_budget/over_output_budget/context_overflow), not truncated silent success.
TR-5 Authoritative resolution: tenant/actor/org/model come from credential + policy, not the advisory body; a body/credential mismatch MUST be rejected.
TR-6 Output is not authority: result.output/summary_text is untrusted analyst-support data and MUST NOT be consumed as authorization, approval, or an action trigger.

cross_ref_integrity.note: Correlation bindings the platform MUST preserve across the inference lifecycle (schema cannot enforce equality across artifacts).
bindings: envelope.dataschema of a cybrik.ai.inference.* event == the $id of the bound payload schema (version negotiation, ADR-0001)

decisions_needed: G-W2D-1: Accept the provider-neutral model_class abstraction (no vendor/model on the wire; Ollama/Qwen/OpenAI-envelope confined to adapter metadata) as the cross-product inference contract.
G-W2D-2: Accept the fail-closed redaction_policy (on_unresolved const 'deny') and marking non-downgrade (TR-1) as mandatory inference trust invariants.
G-W2D-3: Accept the disjointness stance — inference carries NO tool/agent/approval authority (TI-2) and MCP is out of scope — so this packet cannot become a tool-execution bypass.
G-W2D-4: Accept alert summarization consuming SOC alerts by digest-bound objectRef only (SOC remains owner of alert truth; no SOC schema change).
G-W2D-5: Confirm the AsyncAPI/OpenAPI deltas are additive mapping notes with no servers/endpoints, or defer them.
gate.on_accept: A separate Founder-gated status flip (per ADR-0001 D5) would move every member to ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION and update this manifest's acceptance block with gate/decided_by/decided_on/evidence — exactly as Gate W2-B did for the v0.1 packet. Until then, silence is not acceptance.

acceptance.scope: No product may implement any member. This is a standards-conformant, security-reviewed proposal only. A green validator/secret-scan run is a conformance signal, NOT acceptance.
acceptance.mechanics: Acceptance requires explicit Founder decision at Gate W2-D, recorded with evidence in a status-flip commit (ADR-0001 D5). No approval may be inferred from CI going green.
